bull_bear.body: Dividend proposed: INR240/share (37% of profits); leverage maintained below 1x; capex fully funded by operating cash flows; no external funding planned; cash returned to shareholders as confidence in earnings quality and growth pipeline
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: West Asia fuel/bag cost volatility; rupee depreciation (non-cash forex impact); rural demand sensitivity to monsoon/crop outcomes; industry fragmentation limiting pricing power; legacy legal issues delaying ICL merger
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, execution-focused, proud of delivery on all commitments (capacity, brand migration, cost targets); tone is assured, not defensive; emphasized consistency and discipline as core identity
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: India Cements' underlying EBITDA is ~INR670/ton (not INR497) due to tolling arrangement — marketing/distribution costs are borne by UltraTech; RMC is a strategic future engine, not a monetizable asset; 1.54x clinker ratio target implies continued OPC dominance despite industry trends; no impact on dispatches despite bag cost spike — supply chain resilience
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- FY26 free cash flow to firm was negative ₹136 Crores, reflecting heavy reinvestment with operating cash flow of only ₹3 Crores.
- Net debt increased to ₹1,271 Crores from ₹1,135 Crores YoY, supporting the growth capex cycle.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: India Cements: 3.12M tons Q4 volume, 2.73M tons UltraTech-branded (87%), EBITDA INR497/ton (up from INR305/ton in Q3), capex INR1,992cr total for efficiency + expansion; Kesoram: Operating at INR1,000+/ton EBITDA; UAE: 5M tons capacity, EBITDA INR278cr in Q4, stable QoQ; RMC: Integral to business model, no monetization planned
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Brand migration completed in March 2026, signaling a unified go-to-market identity.
- Trade sales mix improved to 75% in Q4 FY26 from 59% in Q4 FY25, indicating a strategic shift toward higher-margin retail channels.

deepdive.thesis: UltraTech crossed 200M tons capacity ahead of schedule, completed 100% brand migration of India Cements and Kesoram, and achieved EBITDA per ton of INR1,253 despite bag cost spikes and forex losses, with integration now turning from drag to accretion and setting a clear path to INR1,000+ EBITDA/ton for acquired assets by FY28

open.item: With prices improving in South markets from April, India Cements performance will improve further.

Fuel costs rose slightly to INR1.8/kCal this quarter; India Cements EBITDA dampened by shutdowns/maintenance and Tamil Nadu limestone royalty, though management expects ~INR100/ton of maintenance cost to reverse in Q3.
Management expects South India pricing to stabilize with upward bias driven by large institutional demand (Amravati, data centers, IT); calls FY26 a "fabulous year."
Management asserts India Cements will be a strong company at par with modern plants within 2-3 years driven by cost-cutting on pyro-processing, limestone, heat generation and coolers.
West Asia conflict flagged as a real near-term headwind on fuel, packing bags (up ~INR6/bag) and freight; UltraTech says price increases already taken in April are expected to offset the cost impact.
India Cements brand conversion crossed 58% at end of December '25 (Kesoram 69%); both to complete brand transition by June '26.
India Cements brand transition at 31% complete (Sept '25), to cross 40% by December quarter; both acquired brands (ICL & Kesoram) to complete transition not later than June '26.
Group expects sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum and targets double-digit growth for FY27; industry demand grew ~6-7% in Q4FY26 (~6.5% full year FY26).
India Cements EBITDA per ton (INR400 in Q3) targeted to reach INR1,000 exit by Q4FY27, driven by brand conversion, price hikes and the efficiency capex program.
India Cements cost-improvement capex committed INR601 crore, of which INR144 crore spent so far; benefits to start reflecting in the P&L from January-March '27.
India Cements + Kesoram brand transition to UltraTech to be completed (100%) before the end of fiscal '27.

India Cements capex plan of ~INR1,500 crore (INR1,000 crore towards WHRS and profit-improvement) with payback <3 years, to be spent in FY26 and FY27; benefits reflecting from the Jan-March '27 quarter.
India Cements brand to be fully transitioned into UltraTech (via tolling + rebranding) by end of fiscal '27.
WHRS additions from acquired assets: ~22 MW for India Cements (ICL) plus ~24 MW for Kesoram, to be added to the network by FY27.

Group-wide cost/efficiency improvement of upwards of INR300 per ton to be delivered over the 3-year window by FY27 (INR86/ton already delivered by FY25); India Cements/Kesoram efficiency programs run in parallel.
India Cements capex program details (WHRS, cooler upgrades, alternate fuel) to be formally shared next quarter; work slated for mid-FY26 to FY27 with P&L benefits from Q1FY28 (April-June '27).
UltraTech crossed 200 million tons India capacity (a year ahead of target); committed to add a further 37 million tons to exceed 242.5 million tons by fiscal '28.
India Cements cost-improvement capex benefits to fully convert into efficiency improvement in the January-March '28 quarter (~INR200/ton).
India Cements to cross INR1,000 EBITDA per ton by end of fiscal '28, backed by INR1,592 cr efficiency capex + INR400 cr capacity capex and ~INR200/ton further efficiency improvement.
India Cements Dalavoi/Chennai brownfield is grinding capacity (0.4 mt in Tamil Nadu); no further clinker capacity added there as clinker is available in-region.
